correctness.rationale: For n≥4, 3≤k≤n−1, any linear vertex-data right inverse corresponds to signed coefficient measures of mass 1; on unit equilateral vertices KR dual norm is half the ℓ1 difference. Averaging over S_n does not increase norm, so arbitrary minimization reduces to one equivariant pair a,b with ka+(n−k)b=1. Euclidean chord distances of inside-vertex, outside-vertex and face pairs give A(b)=(k−1+(n−k)b)/(kp), B(b)=(1−b)/q, C(b)=√r(1−nb), plus 1, p=√((k−1)/(2k)), q=√((k+1)/(2k)), r=min(k,n−k). Signed b outside [0,1/n] cannot improve; crossing A/B when r=1 and A/C when r≥2 gives two exact piecewise formulas and positive weights. Derivatives in n show each fixed-k supremum is strict n→∞ limit L_k=k√k/(1+k√((k−1)/2)). Differentiating h(k)=√(1−1/k)+√2 k^(−3/2) finds continuous minimum at 9+3√7 in (16,17), and exact rational radical bounds distinguish integer 17 from 16. Independently enumerated every point pair for all 21 (n,k) with n=4..9; obtained exact predicted optimum. General result follows from symmetry/duality/analytic inequalities, not finite enumeration.
